resources.name: WeHeY
quotes: We present a system, WeHeY, built atop WeHe, that can localize traffic differentiation, i.e., obtain concrete evidence that the differentiation happened within the client’s ISP.
WeHeY’s source code is publicly available at https://nal-epfl.github.io/WeHeY.
references: Zeinab Shmeis, Muhammad Abdullah, Pavlos Nikolopoulos, Katerina Argyraki, David Choffnes, and Phillipa Gill. 2023. Localizing Traffic Differentiation. In Proceedings of the 2023 ACM Internet Measurement Conference (IMC ’23), October 24–26, 2023, Montreal, QC, Canada.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: The paper presents WeHeY as the primary system being designed, implemented, and evaluated.

resources.name: WeHe
quotes: We present a system, WeHeY, built atop WeHe, that can localize traffic differentiation
WeHe [23] tests whether a network provider provides differential performance for a supported set of services (e.g., Skype, WhatsApp, Webex, Netflix, Zoom, etc.).
references: Fangfan Li, Arian Akhavan Niaki, David Choffnes, Phillipa Gill, and Alan Mislove. 2019. A large-scale analysis of deployed traffic differentiation practices. In Proceedings of the ACM Special Interest Group on Data Communication.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: WeHeY is built on top of WeHe, and WeHe is used to detect the initial traffic differentiation before WeHeY localizes it.

resources.name: CAIDA Anonymized Internet Traces Dataset
quotes: In addition to the trace replays, we send along the two paths background traffic generated from CAIDA Internet traces [4].
references: CAIDA. 2023. The CAIDA Anonymized Internet Traces Dataset (April 2008 - January 2019). https://www.caida.org/catalog/datasets/passive_dataset/. Accessed August 2023.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: The authors use this dataset to generate background traffic for their emulation and simulation experiments.

resources.name: RouteViews
